parsed.rationale: Both `HSBColor.uiColor` (line 53) and `HSBColor.nsColor` (line 63) are computed properties in the same file (`Shared/ColorPalette/Sources/ColorPalette/HSBColor.swift`) within the `ColorPalette` package, with a Jaccard similarity of 0.71, indicating substantial shared body logic (likely the same HSB component extraction). They cannot be merged into one property because they target different platform color types. Extracting a private `colorComponents()` or `makeBaseColor()` helper eliminates the duplicated conversion arithmetic while preserving the two distinct public-facing properties. No context flags (test, codegen, mock, sample-app) suggest the duplication is intentional.

specifics.proposed_action: Introduce a private helper method on `HSBColor` (e.g., `func makeColor(usingUIColor: Bool) -> AnyObject` or, more idiomatically, a shared `func colorComponents() -> (hue: CGFloat, saturation: CGFloat, brightness: CGFloat, alpha: CGFloat)`) that encapsulates the shared HSB-to-color conversion logic. Both `uiColor` and `nsColor` computed properties would then delegate to this helper, each wrapping the result in the platform-appropriate type (`UIColor` vs `NSColor`). The helper should live in the same file, `Shared/ColorPalette/Sources/ColorPalette/HSBColor.swift`, immediately above the two properties.
specifics.why_no_category_fits: The two properties (`HSBColor.uiColor` at line 53 and `HSBColor.nsColor` at line 63) are near-duplicates (Jaccard 0.71) that must remain as two distinct computed properties because they return platform-specific types (`UIColor` and `NSColor`).
